answer: Unique Work Replay Ledger. Each identity must submit a task whose solution depends on a secret seed issued once, and the ledger stores only a hash of the output; replaying any prior answer is rejected because the seed differs. An attacker farming identities must solve a fresh raven task per identity. The hollow seed space prevents stockpiling. To reach a summit of N valid agents, the attacker pays N distinct compute costs plus storage, since copied outputs fail hash checks.
